This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 24-05-2024 at about 11:45 p.m., the petitioner was traveling in a Tata Sumo vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ- 1468, towards his village Balaganatham from Kyasamballi village.

At that time, near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village,
Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, the driver of said Tata Sumo namely Srinivasulu Reddy drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road side tree.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner got stuck inside the vehicle and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to PES Hospital, Kuppam, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident he was working as mason and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Ramakuppam Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Tata Sumo for the offence punishable under Section 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of Private Car package policy bearing No.0516033123P116864129 in respect of Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 and it was valid from 17-03-2024 to 16-03-2025.

Further it is contended that, the driver of the Tata Sumo vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MJ-1468 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.1/owner of said vehicle being aware of the same has consciously allowed such person to drive his vehicle and thereby committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further, it has sought for Purushotham Reddy K vs Harish A on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195780985/
2 permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

sentences.text: Further it is contended that, the respondent No.1/owner of the Tata Sumo had allowed or permitted his driver to drive the said vehicle in the public place without a valid fitness certificate.
As such, the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and had acted in contravention of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988.
Further it is contended that, the said accident has occurred due to contributory negligence of the petitioner.

The accident having occurred at around 11.45 p.m., during the night hours, on a busy road, near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village,
Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh.
The petitioner had not taken reasonable care for the safety of himself, as well as the driver of the vehicle.
The act of the petitioner in having taken the risk of engaging the driver in conversion, has led him to jump the vehicle and it has resulted in the accident.

The petitioner is liable for contributory negligence for not less than 75%
and he is "author of his own wrong".
Hence, the compensation if any awarded to the petitioner is to be reduced by 75% having contributed to the accident.
Further, it has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 24-05-2024 at about 11.45 p.m., near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the TATA SUMO bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MJ-1468 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

sentences.text: Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 24-05-2024 at about 11.45 p.m., when he was traveling in a Tata Sumo vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468, near Green Valley School,
Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, at that time the driver of offending Tata Sumo drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road side tree.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner got stuck inside the vehicle and sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident he was working as mason and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of her oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 and 2(a) are true copy of first information statement and its translated copy, Ex.P.3 and 3(a) are true copy of sketch and its translated copy, Ex.P.4 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.5 is true copy of charge- sheet, Ex.P.6 and 7 are discharge summary (total 2), Ex.P.8 are OPD slips (total 2), Ex.P.9 is notarized copy of Aadhar card of petitioner, Ex.P.10 are medical bills (total 19), Ex.P.11 are prescriptions (total 4) and Ex.P.12 is notarized copy of Aadhar card.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 5, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 and dashing the same to the road side tree.

Due to said impact, the petitioner being inmate of said car has sustained grievous injuries i.e. acute SAH in bilateral tentorium, and laceration of size 3x1x1 c.m., over left lateral side of tongue and multiple grade abrasions over face.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.5,
has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-MJ-1468.
12.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 in the accident, the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and has taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place due to the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner, as he had engaged the driver of said vehicle in conversion with him and the same led to the accident.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any evidence, nor it has produced any document to establish the above contentions.

Even,
the respondent No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 and dashing the same to the road side tree.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing Purushotham Reddy K vs Harish A on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195780985/
4 worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to his own negligence or there was any contributory negligence on his part, in the cause of accident.

Further, the Ex.P.3 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the right side of the road, near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, due to dashing of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 to the road side tree.
Further, it is not the case of the respondent No.2 that, the accident has taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MJ-1468 involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.5 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-MJ-1468 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468.

In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.4 wound certificate, Ex.P.6 & 7 discharge summaries and Ex.P.8 OPD slips, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
He has suffered acute SAH in bilateral tentorium and laceration of size 3x1x1 c.m., over left lateral side of tongue and multiple grade abrasions over face.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained acute SAH in bilateral tentorium and laceration of size 3x1x1 c.m., over left lateral side of tongue and multiple grade abrasions over face.

Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. Towards loss of future income:
The petitioner has deposed that, earlier to the accident he was working as mason and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor examined any doctor to establish that, due to injuries sustained in the accident he has suffered any physical disability or deformity.

The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability and he is not in a position to continue his avocation or perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his earning capacity.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
20. Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.1,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 19 medical bills, as per Ex.P.10.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent an amount of Rs.83,647/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.83,647/- under the head of medical expenses.
21. Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e., acute SAH in bilateral tentorium and laceration of size 3x1x1 c.m., over left lateral side of tongue and multiple grade abrasions over face and for the said injuries the petitioner has taken conservative treatment.

As per Ex.P.6 and 7 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 6 days, from 24-05-2024 to 29-05-2024 in PES Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Hospital, Kuppam and Silicon City Hospital, Bengaluru.

25. Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as mason and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do work and continue his avocation.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2024.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month.

The petitioner has taken treatment for 6 days as in-patient at PES Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Hospital,
Kuppam and Silicon City Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries caused to him.

, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,80,947/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
29. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-01-MJ-1468.
The insurance policy bearing No.0516033123P116864129, issued by the respondent No.2, in respect of offending Tata Sumo bearing No.KA-01-MJ-1468, was valid from 17-03-2024 to 16-03-2025.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 24-05-2024.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1/insured.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Therefore,
the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,80,947/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization,
from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 24-05-2024 at about 11.45 p.m., near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the TATA SUMO bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MJ-1468 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, it is not the case of the respondent No.2 that, the accident has taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MJ-1468 involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.5 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-MJ-1468 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor examined any doctor to establish that, due to injuries sustained in the accident he has suffered any physical disability or deformity.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2024.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1/insured.
Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 the accident in question has taken place.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
opennyai_summary.arguments: The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability and he is not in a position to continue his avocation or perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his earning capacity.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, no compensation is awarded under this particular head.
28. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Nil 2.
Medical expenses Rs. 83,647-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4. Attendant charges 6,000-00
Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during 16,500-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,80,947/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
Therefore,
the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,80,947/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization,
from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,80,947/- (Rupees one lakh eighty thousand nine hundred and forty seven only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment, on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
